To implement Kaminari pagination, ensure the gem is installed and the scope of your collection is defined as an ActiveRecord relation. ```ruby # config/routes.rb Rails.application.routes.draw do resources :articles, only: [:index, :show] end # app/controllers/articles_controller.rb class ArticlesController < ApplicationController def index # Use .page(params[:page]) to hook into Kaminari logic # and .per(10) to set the limit. @articles = Article.all.page(params[:page]).per(10) end end # app/views/articles/index.html.erb <%# @articles is now a Kaminari::ActionPager object %>

Articles

<% @articles.each do |article| %> <% end %>
<%= article.title %> <%= article.content %>
<%# Helper provided by Kaminari to render pagination links %> <%= paginate_partial @articles %> ``` ### Key Implementation Details: 1. **ActiveRecord Relation**: Ensure `Article.all` (or your specific scope) is not converted into an Array before calling `.page`, as Kaminari needs the relation to inject the SQL `LIMIT` and `OFFSET`. 2. **Default Scope**: If you prefer a global default, you can move `.per(10)` to a scope in the model: `scope :default_page, -> { per(10) }` and call `@articles = Article.default_page.page(params[:page])`. 3. **Helper**: The `paginate_partial` (or `paginate` depending on your Kaminari version/config) helper automatically generates the "Next", "Previous", and page number links based on the current request params.
